findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an owner accepts a review finding after the code's tests pass.
The Done-when is: “A close or land round pushes its code and its review record together, so a records-only push no longer cancels a CI run of the same code, and a later records-only head reuses that run's green result”. Acceptance changes both the review and its `known` findings (`src/forge/close.py:138` and `src/forge/score.py:168`), but `.forge/review-tests.py:203-218` rejects changes to `known`. It therefore reruns the suite despite the green parent. It also rejects status-only records and review commits that include `plans/spotted` records. If the previous run is still active, `.github/workflows/forge.yml:11-13` cancels it. The branch leaves these paths unchanged.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - this pull request reaches its required tests check.
The proof list relies on the close, parent-reuse, test-receipt, and acceptance tests, but the PR check runs `forge test --change` (`.github/workflows/forge.yml:82`). For this diff, the selector at `src/forge/fasttest.py:352-400` and `:711-718` selects tests related to the timing and fix-record files; none of those four proof files is selected or listed in `.forge/always-tests.txt`. The required check can therefore pass without running the claimed behavioral proofs.
findings.title: Gate: proof list

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a green run is followed by the owner's acceptance of a finding.
The named reuse proof hand-writes a simplified review record (`tests/test_review_record_reuses_parent_tests.py:77-101`); the receipt proof similarly constructs its state by hand. Neither produces the `known` change made by a real acceptance, so both pass while that records-only head reruns the suite. The acceptance proof checks the review gate, not test reuse. Cover the actual close-generated record through the CI entry point for a new and an earlier-adopted client.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_review_record_reuses_parent_tests.py

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a new or earlier-adopted client closes or lands a code change.
The named close proof counts remote updates and checks the pull request body (`tests/test_close_publishes_final_review_once.py:40-50`), but does not check that the pushed head contains a valid review; a code-only push with a clean body would pass it. There is also no direct land proof of the single reviewed update: `tests/test_land_closes_committed_work.py:63-70` checks the final version and output, not the number or review contents of branch updates. Exercise both commands and check the review gate on the pushed head.
findings.title: Gate: one reviewed push through close and land

why: Half of Forge's pull request CI runs are cancelled, and half of that waste comes from a push that changes only review records and cancels a run of the same code
